article.title: Teens and Nukes
article.author: Mark Bird
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Many high school teens are much smarter than their parents or grandparents think. They can reason that President Trump has repeatedly stated Iran cannot have one nuclear weapon, yet he has apparently done nothing to reduce or eliminate the dozens held by North Korea, the hundreds by China, or the thousands by Russia. When Trump announced plans for a 44% increase in the DoD/DoW budget for 2027, some teens likely thought there should be a 44% decrease. The 44% increase is a proposed miliary budget of $1.5 trillion. Since they passed 4 th grade math, teens can calculate that $1.5 trillion amounts to $4,348 per American [[1.5 trillion divided by 345 million Americans]] or over $10,000 per 3-person home. A teen of below average intellect can certainly ponder the probability that there will be at least a single hostile nuclear explosion in their lifetime or in the lifetime of their future children. Teens have access to Dr. Google with a PhD in everything. Teens and some pre-teens of average aptitude can access any of dozens nuclear weapons websites, including: Bulletin of Atomic Scientists Code Pink Nevada Desert Experience Peace Action Physicians for Social Responsibility The Union of Concerned Scientists Women Against Military Madness In less than a few hours, slightly more ambitious teens they might discover: The world has a little over 10,000 nuclear weapons Humans have made bombs 1,000 times larger than the Hiroshima bomb (15 kiloton versus 15 megaton) Nuclear weapon blast winds spread radioactivity hundreds of MPH About 1,000 square miles near the 1986 Chernobyl power plant disaster are still off-limits [[Source below]] A tiny percent of today’s nuclear weapons could induce planetary nuclear winter. They can ask AI related questions. At the U.S. Navy website, they can learn about the dominance of US aircraft carriers and virtually invulnerable nuclear submarines. From this website and others, they can learn one US sub has the firepower exceeding over 100 Hiroshima bombs. Related: Lake Mead and Lake Powell Are Heading Toward a System Crash Five former teens you probably know Rachel Maddow , as a pre-teen or teen, certainly knew her father had been a US Air Force Captain shortly before her birth. Drift , her first book in 2012, asserted that US military power has gradually “drifted” away from checks and balances. According to the book’s index, pages 216-241 pertain to “nuclear weapons.” Today, Maddow might say checks and balances have eroded in recent years at the pace and size of a tsunami. Another book by her is titled: Prequel: An American Fight Against Fascism. Stephen King and Dean Koontz were precocious teens, are both near age 80, were significantly influenced by Poe, have each written over 60 books, have multiple books pertaining to nuclear holocausts, other books with the word “nuclear,” and have multiple other books with apocalyptic themes. One or both have books with the words “dark, darker, or darkest” in the title. As teens, both King and Koontz were profoundly influenced by the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis. According to King’s website, in 1963 he began writing the unpublished manuscript The Aftermath, which “describes life after a nuclear war.” Koontz’s first novel, Star Quest , was published in 1968 and focuses on planets shattered by warfare. Carl Sagan was born in 1934. As Hiroshima occurred in 1945, he certainly knew plenty as a teen about radioactive implications inherent in Einstein’s E=mc2 formula. Sagan’s best-selling 1980 book, Cosmos, has a map on page 321 depicting radioactive winds blowing across the US. His famous nuclear winter cover story in Parade Magazine appeared in the October 30, 1983 issue. In the mid-1980’s, both King and Koontz used the words “nuclear winter” in novels Greta Thunberg , when age 16, was selected by Time Magazine for its 2019 Person of the Year for addressing the UN and alerting the world to global warming. Time also notes Greta learned about global warming at age 8 and was so depressed about it that she “stopped speaking almost entirely.” Greta said her depression abated when she became an activist. Most teens know of the massive Canadian smoke that impacted over a dozen states in 2026, the record fires in Washington state in 2026, the LA urban fire in 2025 and multiple other disasters partly attributed to climate change. Some might wonder of the implications if such smoke was radioactive. Now every US high school likely has Gretas and Gregs inspired to activism by Thunberg. Every middle school likely has students with budding Greta mentalities. Every high school has students who believe current reality is a horror story far more terrifying than any novel by King or Koontz. All teens have brains with trillions of synaptic connections, communicate with many other teens, are likely in the most curious decade of their lives, and most adult worldviews are patterned in the teen years. Related: Free Will Ideology Is Unscientific New teen consciousness During the 19 th century, most US teens had a farm-related consciousness. In the 1930’s, they had a depression era consciousness. Even if they never heard of Maddow, King, Koontz, Sagan and Thunberg, millions of recent teens, many current teens, and some pre-teens have to some degree, a “MKKST” consciousness. Almost all teens know of the Four Nuclear Horsemen of the Apocalypse. They have heard of the Chinese "leader" who significantly increased his nuclear arsenal in recent years and has threatened nearby nations, the North Korean "leader" who mutually engaged in an over 12-month nuclear confrontation with the current US "leader;" the Russian "leader" who has bombed Ukraine for over 50 months and dozens of times threatened Ukraine with nuclear weapons, and the US "leader" who has threatened over a half dozen nations and also threatened to end the Iranian civilization. Like others, they can wonder about the mental health of the Four Nuclear Horsemen. Even if they have never read a sentence of the Bible, they know it does not say people should lie, steal, and commit adultery. They know it does not say, “Nuke Thy Neighbor.” Now, various degrees of despair may be afflicting over half of all American teens. Teens know they have an inalienable right to expect a healthy planet for themselves and their children. What if 10 percent of teens are intermittent viewers of Maddow and are familiar with one book of one of the five people above, or similar books? What if 1-5 million teens are moderate viewers of Maddow and have read multiple books by the five? A short answer is many will think Congresswoman AOC and NYC Mayor Mamdani are "too conservative" for not verbalizing key solutions to nuclear weapons and other issues. Specifically, teens may be wondering why virtually all DEM and GOP politicians: Do not emphasize that 1% of nukes could induce nuclear winter Do not emphatically state US military spending should be reduced by 25 or 50 percent from the pre-2025 budget Do not propose that all nations should reduce military spending by 10 percent and these funds be devoted to reducing climate change Do not stress that, like the last decade, a rough estimate is there will be another 30 million malnutrition deaths in the next decade. Do not propose legislation that at least a 90% tax should be imposed for anyone making over $725 per hour--or 100 times the federal minimum wage Do not rebuke the US for not enacting universal health care coverage for all children in the last century Do not emphasize that there has been massive financial, ethnic, and gender inequalities in every year of US history. Conclusion Theologians and others rightly instruct that “vanity is a vice.” But there may be exceptions to that maxim. What became of the author who as a pre-teen had several meals with the future Pakistani dictator who funded the “Islamic nuclear bomb” and whose father had an unique role during the Cuban Missile Crisis? Decades ago, the author played a key role in defeating the proposed MX missile system for eastern Nevada and western Utah. This plan was to place nuclear missiles on continually moving 18-wheeled trucks or trains. The amount of land for the system was estimated to be about the size of Connecticut. He also has influenced the actions of leaders in three anti-nuke organizations, spent 30-days in jail for a John Lewis “good trouble” type protest relating to nuclear weapons, and is author of the LAP article “ Good News About Nuclear Winter - LA Progressive ” A new generation of Americans is blossoming. If the planet endures, this emerging new teen consciousness may be the most auspicious trend in US history since 1776. NOTES: The Chernobyl Exclusion Zone (CEZ) — the area with the highest radioactive contamination — covers about 2,600 km² (approximately 1,000 square miles) in Ukraine Wikipedia+1 . This zone was established after the 1986 disaster and remains largely off-limits to the public to prevent exposure and to allow monitoring and cleanup. The U.S. Navy operates 11 nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and a fleet of 66 nuclear submarines, forming the backbone of its global maritime dominance. The United States holds a majority share of the world’s nuclear-powered warships, especially in submarines. The U.S. Navy operates the largest fleet of nuclear submarines in the world Wikipedia .
